components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the oceans, atmosphere and land

components.label: DEPTH 1
components.title: Evaporation
components.body: Heat from the sun warms liquid water at the surface of oceans, lakes and rivers. The water turns into water vapour and rises into the air.

components.label: DEPTH 2
components.title: Condensation
components.body: As water vapour rises, it cools. The vapour condenses around tiny dust and salt particles, forming droplets that gather into clouds.

components.label: DEPTH 3
components.title: Precipitation and collection
components.body: When droplets in a cloud grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow or hail. Water then runs off into rivers or soaks into the ground, and the cycle begins again.
components.takeaway: Precipitation returns water to the land and seas.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Following one raindrop
components.body: A water molecule evaporates from a lake on a warm afternoon. It rises, cools high in the atmosphere, and joins a cloud as part of a droplet. The droplet merges with others and falls as rain on a hillside. It soaks into the soil, seeps into a stream, and flows back to the lake.
components.takeaway: One molecule can complete the whole cycle many times.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens when heat from the sun turns liquid water into vapour.

questions.question: Why does water vapour form clouds?
options: It cools and condenses around particles
It freezes into ice at ground level
It is pushed out by wind
questions.explanation: Cooling vapour condenses around dust and salt particles to form droplets.

questions.question: Which stage returns water to the land and seas?
questions.explanation: Precipitation falls as rain, snow or hail, and collection moves it back to bodies of water.
